analysis:
This batch contains only documentation. It adds changelog.d/coordinator-reconnect-stall.md (head lines 1-4) and edits docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines 3, 443-447 and 1943). The docs describe two behavior changes whose Swift implementation is not in this batch.

(1) A new 30 s coordinator handshake deadline covering TCP, TLS and the WebSocket upgrade. The cited source is CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift (defaultTimeout = 30). A stalled handshake is cancelled and retried with the existing backoff. This is an availability improvement on TB-002 and introduces no new trust. Integration should verify that cancellation tears down the half-open connection. It should also verify that a timed-out handshake cannot leave stale endpoint/grant state, keeping T-053's endpoint-replacement and revocation semantics intact.

(2) Lifecycle drain for stop, restart and start now completes without the coordinator acknowledgement only when no work is left and no coordinator session is registered (cli-reference.md head 443-447). This weakens the documented protocol barrier ('requires the updated coordinator before normal provider shutdown can be confirmed', base line 447-448). Integration must confirm three things in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift (performLifecycleDrain):
- The 'no registered session' check is race-free against a reconnect that registers mid-drain. Otherwise accepted work or terminal usage settlement (billing, A-009) could be skipped.
- 'No unfinished requests' includes pending usage/terminal receipts, not just in-flight inference.
- Logout (A-008, T-053) still stops the process before revocation. Logout uses the same DrainOptions, so the bypass also applies there. That is likely acceptable: no session means no live credential use. It still needs verification that the process-exit confirmation is unchanged.

No security regression is evidenced by the docs alone, and a docs-only change cannot be cited as a defect. Deeper review of the Swift source is needed to validate these contracts.
